title: Abnormal Behavior Of Water
definition: The anomalous expansion of water refers to its unique thermodynamic behavior where, unlike most liquids that continuously contract upon cooling, water contracts until 4°C and then expands as it cools further down to 0°C, reaching maximum density at 4°C.
importanceInUpsc: Tested frequently in UPSC Prelims (GS-1 Physics/General Science) through applied conceptual questions regarding aquatic ecosystem survival, geological weathering (frost wedging), and thermodynamic anomalies. Relevant for Mains GS-3 under Science and Technology applications.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Abnormal Behavior Of Water.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: States of matter and thermal expansion
